title: Spatial contrast sensitivity (Campbell & Robson, 1968)
summary: How faint can a pattern of stripes be and still be seen, and how does that depend on how fine the stripes are? A stationary sine-wave grating in a square field on a uniform grey of the same mean luminance is shown at several spatial frequencies; its threshold contrast is measured at each, and contrast sensitivity (1 / threshold) plotted against frequency is the contrast-sensitivity function. Main task: two-interval forced choice with QUEST+. Second task: the paper's own method of adjustment. A third set compares sine- with square-wave gratings (the paper's Fourier test, 4/pi).
references: Campbell, F. W., & Robson, J. G. (1968). Application of Fourier analysis to the visibility of gratings. The Journal of Physiology, 197(3), 551-566. https://doi.org/10.1113/jphysiol.1968.sp008574
Watson, A. B. (2017). QUEST+: A general multidimensional Bayesian adaptive psychometric method. Journal of Vision, 17(3):10. https://doi.org/10.1167/17.3.10

Allard, R., & Faubert, J. (2008). The noisy-bit method for digital displays: Converting a 256 luminance resolution into a continuous resolution. Behavior Research Methods, 40(3), 735-743. https://doi.org/10.3758/BRM.40.3.735

Lesmes, L. A., Lu, Z.-L., Baek, J., & Albright, T. D. (2010). Bayesian adaptive estimation of the contrast sensitivity function: The quick CSF method. Journal of Vision, 10(3):17. https://doi.org/10.1167/10.3.17

tasks.title: Contrast threshold, two-interval forced choice
tasks.summary: Two looks marked by corner marks; a vertical sine grating is in one of them. F for the first, J for the second. QUEST+ sets the contrast per spatial frequency; the threshold is the 81%-correct contrast of a fitted Weibull function, and sensitivity is its reciprocal.

parameters.name: field_dva
parameters.label: Field size
parameters.meaning: Side of the square grating field. The paper's apertures subtended 10 x 10 deg (57 cm) or 2 x 2 deg (285 cm), p. 553-554.

parameters.name: sf_cpd
parameters.label: Spatial frequencies
parameters.meaning: One cell per frequency (cycles per degree). ASSUMED, not in the paper. The paper covered about 0.1-40 c/deg (Fig. 2).

parameters.name: waveforms
parameters.label: Waveforms
parameters.meaning: sine, or sine and square (the paper's p. 555 comparison); every waveform at every frequency.

parameters.name: orientation_deg
parameters.label: Wave-vector direction
parameters.meaning: 0 = vertical stripes, luminance varying left to right. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: random_phase
parameters.label: Random phase
parameters.meaning: Grating phase drawn uniformly per presentation. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: mean_luminance
parameters.label: Mean luminance
parameters.meaning: Mean grey of the field and the whole screen, as a fraction of the display's maximum after gamma linearisation; snapped to a code value. ASSUMED, not in the paper. The paper's mean was 500 cd/m2.

parameters.name: display_bits
parameters.label: Display bit depth
parameters.meaning: Code depth per channel of the rig's display; sets the quantisation the realised contrast is computed with. Set it to your display's. ASSUMED, not in the paper.
